question: An abortion is medically defined as the termination of a pregnancy before which gestational week?
explanation: Medical guidelines classify any pregnancy loss or termination occurring before 20 completed weeks of gestation as an abortion. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T008#GNS226_U5_T008_h1)

question: What is the main clinical difference between an inevitable abortion and a threatened abortion?
explanation: An inevitable abortion involves an open cervix, meaning the pregnancy cannot be saved, whereas a threatened abortion has a closed cervix. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T008#GNS226_U5_T008_h1)

question: What is the first nursing action when a patient comes in with heavy bleeding after an abortion?

options.B: Send blood for grouping and crossmatching

explanation: Checking vital signs helps detect shock and unstable blood pressure before moving on to other treatments. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T008#GNS226_U5_T008_h2)

question: During an incomplete abortion, why is a speculum examination performed?

options.B: Retained tissue in the cervical os

explanation: Looking through a speculum helps identify pregnancy tissue stuck in the cervical opening that is causing ongoing bleeding. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T008#GNS226_U5_T008_h2)

question: Which intravenous cannula size is best for quick fluid replacement in a bleeding patient?
explanation: Large-bore cannulas allow fluids and blood to flow rapidly to treat low blood volume effectively. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T008#GNS226_U5_T008_h3)

question: Why are broad-spectrum antibiotics given before clearing a septic abortion?

options.A: To shrink the size of the enlarged uterus
options.B: To prevent bacteremic shock during manipulation
options.C: To stop excessive uterine bleeding instantly
options.D: To replace the need for surgical intervention

explanation: Surgical tools can push bacteria into the bloodstream, so antibiotics must be given first to prevent widespread infection. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T008#GNS226_U5_T008_h3)

question: What is the main effect of misoprostol when used for a medical abortion?
explanation: Misoprostol softens the cervix and causes the uterus to contract so it can empty its contents. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T008#GNS226_U5_T008_h4)

question: A patient having a medical abortion reports mild shivering and cramping after taking misoprostol. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Reassure the patient as these are normal side effects
options.B: Prepare the operating theatre immediately for a laparotomy
options.C: Stop all further medication doses and give IV epinephrine
options.D: Report suspected septic shock to the senior doctor on call

explanation: Mild fever and shivering are common side effects of prostaglandin medications and usually pass on their own. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T008#GNS226_U5_T008_h4)

question: Which tool is the main feature of Manual Vacuum Aspiration (MVA)?
explanation: MVA uses a specialized handheld syringe attached to a plastic tube to create suction. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T008#GNS226_U5_T008_h5)

question: Why is Manual Vacuum Aspiration often chosen over metal curettage for early incomplete abortions?

options.A: It carries a lower risk of uterine perforation
options.B: It can be safely performed up to 28 weeks gestation
options.C: It does not require any form of pain relief
options.D: It completely eliminates the need for nursing supervision

explanation: Flexible plastic tubes are much less likely to puncture the muscular wall of the uterus compared to sharp metal instruments. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T008#GNS226_U5_T008_h5)

question: How soon can a woman start ovulating again after an early abortion?

options.B: Only after the next normal menses

explanation: The ovaries bounce back quickly, meaning a woman can get pregnant again before her next period starts. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T008#GNS226_U5_T008_h6)

question: What is the main goal of adding family planning counseling to Post-Abortion Care?

options.A: Evaluating the exact cause of the initial miscarriage
options.C: Treating underlying chronic pelvic inflammatory disease
options.D: Complying with mandatory hospital admission rules

explanation: Family planning helps women choose contraceptives to avoid quick repeat unplanned pregnancies and unsafe procedures. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T008#GNS226_U5_T008_h6)

question: Which complication requires emergency surgery via a laparotomy?
explanation: A hole in the uterus, especially if it might affect the bowel or bladder, needs immediate surgery to prevent severe infection and bleeding. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T008#GNS226_U5_T008_h7)

question: A patient develops foul-smelling vaginal discharge and lower belly pain after an abortion procedure. What should the nurse suspect?
explanation: Foul discharge and pelvic pain are classic signs of an uterine infection that need prompt antibiotic treatment. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T008#GNS226_U5_T008_h7)

question: Under Nigerian criminal law, when is an induced abortion legally permitted?

options.A: Severe financial hardship of the family
options.B: When pregnancy results from consensual dating
options.D: To save the life of the mother

explanation: Nigerian law only allows pregnancy termination if continuing the pregnancy directly threatens the woman's life. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T008#GNS226_U5_T008_h8)

question: How should a nurse handle personal beliefs when caring for a patient with complications from an unsafe abortion?

options.A: Provide emergency life-saving care without judgment
options.B: Report the patient to local law enforcement immediately
options.C: Refuse to touch the patient until she confesses
options.D: Delay treatment until a colleague with similar views arrives

explanation: Nurses must put patient safety first and provide emergency care professionally, regardless of personal opinions. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T008#GNS226_U5_T008_h8)
